State Parliament and local councils: different responsibilities.

Legislative Assembly: 88 districts elect one MP each. Legislative Council: eight regions elect five MLCs each; each region contains 11 Assembly districts. The two state layers describe Parliament. The local-council and ward layers describe municipal government.

Local-government councils are separate municipalities. Choose Local councils for 79 municipalities and eight separately labelled unincorporated areas. Choose a council to drill into its wards, current representation and dated population history. The Council regions layer above is the state upper house. VEC: how districts and regions fit together.

    Five members in every Council region

    One labelled badge per current member. Hover a badge for their name, or open the region for its full member list. No region is assigned a single party.

    Country, community and statutory recognition

    Start with First Peoples’ own sources

    Country and language are not defined by the government polygons below. Follow community-led knowledge through Gambay’s First Languages Map, the Victorian Aboriginal Corporation for Languages and the Federation of Victorian Traditional Owner Corporations. Their maps are linked, not copied or traced.

    Separate public statutory layers

    RAP appointments concern statutory cultural-heritage responsibilities. Settlement polygons show agreement extents, not identical rights on every parcel. Neither is a comprehensive Country, language or ownership map. Overlapping records are retained: click to inspect every match. No record in a layer does not mean no Country or Traditional Owners.

    Geometry retrieved 2 October 2026. Catalogue metadata: RAP 15 September 2026; settlements 30 July 2026. Registration, commencement and feature-version dates appear in individual records. No sensitive heritage-site data was accessed. Native-title claims/determinations remain separate official source links, not imported geometry.

    Understanding representation

    Inside the chambers

    Explore the building’s actual member positions, independently drawn from Parliament’s seating sources. Hover for a name; click for a deeper representative profile. Presiding officers are included as members.

    Gallery perspective · Front and presiding officer at the top. On narrow screens, scroll the seating plan horizontally; names remain keyboard accessible.

      What does a majority mean?

      45 of 88 Assembly seats and 21 of 40 Council seats are majorities of all seats. These markers do not say how many votes every motion needs. Ordinary decisions depend on the majority of members voting; attendance, abstentions and special rules can affect the outcome.

      In the Assembly, the Speaker votes only to break a tie. In the Council, the President has an ordinary vote and a tied motion fails. A party's current seat count is not a guarantee of how its members will vote. Government depends on the confidence of the Assembly; a minority government can hold that confidence. Parliament: government and member roles.

      The election ahead

      Dates you can act on

      Enrolment closes 3 November, 8 pm. Candidate nominations run from 4 November, 9 am to 9 November, noon. Early voting runs 18-27 November; election day is 28 November 2026. All times are Melbourne local time.

      VEC 2026 election calendar · checked 2 October 2026.

      Members and candidates are different records

      This directory shows 87 sitting Assembly members, one vacancy and 40 Council members. Brunswick is vacant following Tim Read’s death on 19 September 2026. No final 2026 candidate list is presented; party announcements are not formal nominations.

      Brunswick vacancy source · Parliament member directory

      2026 Council voting: group voting tickets have been removed. Number at least five boxes, in order of preference, either above or below the line. Current VEC instructions. Historical 2022 Council results reflect the rules at that election.

      Local government: coverage and dates

      79 councils, separately from Parliament

      Official Vicmap municipal polygons retain eight unincorporated areas as separate records. Ward edition 2024 includes wards, unsubdivided electoral areas and source exceptions. Current councillor listings and vacancies come from VEC; Moira’s administrator panel is sourced separately. No party affiliations are inferred.

      Council data, topology notes, exact source fields and provenance

      History without false comparisons

      ABS estimated resident population provides annual values for 2001-2025 on ABS LGA 2025 statistical geography, which approximates legal boundaries. Council profiles show the dates and definitions. Financial figures are unavailable pending an accessible source and verified reuse terms. Federal geometry is not yet included.

      ABS population release · VEC council register

      Evidence, with its dates attached

      Actual boundaries, unchanged coordinates

      The map uses full-resolution Vicmap Admin Assembly and Council polygons from the 2020-21 redivision, effective 1 November 2022. Islands, holes and shared edges are retained. The same polygon paths are used to render and select each electorate. Coordinates are projected together; no hand-drawn boundaries or decorative map shapes are used.

      Assembly geometry · Council geometry · Download provenance and checksums

      Attribution: State of Victoria (Victorian Electoral Commission), Vicmap Admin. CC BY 4.0. Retrieved 2 October 2026; projected for display without simplification. This P4A workbench is not an official electoral service.

      Current people, historical observations

      Representation is a snapshot of Parliament’s official member CSV retrieved 2 October 2026, cross-checked with Assembly and Council membership lists. Historical results are linked to their original elections, including Narracan’s 2023 supplementary election and later by-elections.

      Parliament’s Census cards describe the 2021 Census on 2022 boundaries. They are not 2026 population estimates. Each district profile includes seven verified workbook fields with exact source cells. Council regions show their constituent districts; medians are never averaged. Volunteering and rented-tenure percentages are withheld pending verification of their denominators. No electorate-level budget or debt allocation is inferred.
